title: An Empirical Study of the Geometry and Latent-Space Composition of Hypernetwork-Generated LoRAs
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: Generated adapters occupy a compact region of adapter space, while directly trained adapters spread diffusely in broad shells around them.
layout: 2 side-by-side scatter panels, one per model, shared legend style, color-coded clusters
description: Two side-by-side 2-D scatter plots from metric MDS, titled Gemma-2B (left) and Qwen3-8B (right). Axes are labeled MDS dim 1 and MDS dim 2, with light grid lines. In each panel, blue points (NTP-FT) and green points (QA-SFT) form a broad ring or crescent. Red points (hypernetwork output, D2L on the left and SHINE on the right) sit in a distinct compact region. On the left, the red points fill a loose disk inside the ring. On the right, they form a tight dense blob offset from the crescent. A legend in the lower-left corner of each panel names the methods. The eye goes first to the red cluster, which contrasts sharply with the surrounding blue and green shell.
caption: Hypernetwork-generated LoRAs occupy a qualitatively different region of adapter space. We visualize pairwise distances between unit-Frobenius-normalized adapters using metric MDS, with 500 passages per method sampled from the SQuAD validation set. In the two-dimensional MDS embedding, directly fine-tuned NTP-FT and QA-SFT adapters form broad shells, while D2L and SHINE adapters concentrate in compact regions. This structural difference motivates latent merging methods that respect the hypernetwork-induced adapter geometry.
abstract: Recent work proposes hypernetworks that convert a document into a low-rank parameter update (LoRA) in a single forward pass, enabling fast injection of new knowledge into a frozen LLM. However, storing separate LoRA adapters for each document can be unsustainable in streaming settings. In this paper, we study the problem of composing hypernetwork-generated LoRAs using two representative systems, Doc-to-LoRA and SHINE. We show that hypernetwork-generated LoRAs have a geometry sharply different from directly fine-tuned LoRAs. They exhibit greater spectral concentration and stronger cross-document alignment than next-token prediction and QA fine-tuned adapters, which are diffuse and nearly orthogonal across documents. Guided by this observation, we propose latent-space LoRA merging. We compose the intermediate hypernetwork latents and then decode the merged latent through the frozen LoRA-generation head. We show that latent-space merging techniques consistently improve over weight-space and factor-space baselines while preserving a single fixed-rank adapter. These results support latent-space composition as a promising mechanism for combining hypernetwork-generated LoRAs under a fixed output-rank budget.
